extra_misconceptions.fact: Rotating machinery can snag glove fabric and pull fingers into the tool, so bare hands are required near spinning shop equipment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Heavy canvas or leather work gloves protect a mechanic's hands when operating spinning drill presses, lathes, or bench grinders.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hydraulic seals and hoses can fail without warning, so rigid jack stands or mechanical cylinder stops must support raised loads.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hydraulic valves alone hold a raised tractor loader or implement safely in place while a mechanic crawls underneath for repairs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Everyday lenses can shatter on impact and lack side shields, whereas ANSI Z87.1 safety glasses and face shields stop flying debris.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard prescription eyeglasses provide sufficient eye protection when grinding metal or hammering hardened pins in a farm shop.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Diesel and gasoline exhaust rapidly reaches lethal levels indoors unless routed outside through a dedicated exhaust hose or open bays.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Running a tractor engine inside a farm shop with the walk-in door cracked open vents enough exhaust to prevent carbon monoxide buildup.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to wear leather work gloves while operating a high-speed rotating drill press or bench grinder?
Where should a Scout position the ABC fire extinguisher and eyewash station on a farm shop floor plan for emergency access?
What happens to a raised hydraulic loader boom if a mechanic works underneath it without installing cylinder safety locks?
Which physical indicator on a pair of safety glasses confirms they meet impact standards for heavy farm shop repair work?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Diesel engines ignite fuel strictly through the high heat of compressed air, while glow plugs only warm cold cylinders at startup.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Glow plugs in a diesel tractor engine fire on every power stroke just like spark plugs in a gasoline engine to ignite the fuel.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A hydraulic pump produces fluid flow only, and system pressure builds only when that flow encounters resistance from a load or valve.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hydraulic pumps generate system pressure directly regardless of whether any load or resistance is connected to the actuator.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Higher gears trade torque for speed, while lower reduction gears multiply engine torque at the axle to pull heavy tillage implements.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Shifting a tractor transmission into a higher road gear increases both ground speed and maximum drawbar pulling torque at the wheels.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Liquid hydraulic oil is nearly incompressible, which allows it to transmit force instantaneously and rigidly through sealed lines.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hydraulic fluid compresses significantly under heavy loads to act as a natural shock absorber inside tractor lifting cylinders.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the air inside a diesel engine cylinder during the compression stroke to ignite fuel without a spark plug?
Under what condition does Pascal's law allow a small hydraulic pump piston to lift a heavy multi-ton agricultural planter?
What measurement confirms the torque multiplication ratio when a small input gear drives a larger output gear in a transmission?
Why is it dangerous to run a tractor power takeoff shaft at 1,000 RPM when the attached implement is rated only for 540 RPM?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A tapered tip cams out of the slot under torque and strips the fastener, so the blade faces must be filed nearly parallel and flat.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Filing a flat-blade screwdriver tip to a sharp, tapered wedge helps it wedge tightly into different sizes of slotted screw heads.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water swells wood temporarily but crushes the cellular fibers, leaving the handle looser than before once the wood dries out again.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Soaking a loose wooden axe or hammer head in a bucket of water permanently swells the wood fibers to secure the tool head.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Six radial head markings identify a heat-treated Grade 8 bolt, which has roughly double the tensile strength of an unmarked Grade 2 bolt.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Grade 2 and Grade 8 hex bolts of the same diameter and thread pitch can be mixed in one bin because they have identical strength.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Filing a slight bevel around the perimeter of the struck head directs hammer force inward and slows future metal mushrooming.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Grinding a cold chisel's struck head completely flat with sharp 90-degree edges prevents the steel from mushrooming again.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to strike a cold chisel that has a curled, mushroomed metal lip around its struck head?
What measurement confirms that a newly dressed flat-blade screwdriver tip fits the fastener slot without camming out under torque?
Which physical indicator on a replacement hickory hammer handle shows proper grain orientation to resist snapping under impact?
What happens to a hand file's cutting teeth if you drag the blade backward under heavy pressure during the return stroke?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Over-greasing a sealed bearing pops the protective rubber lip seal, allowing abrasive field dust and moisture to enter the race.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pumping grease into every sealed bearing until grease bursts out past the rubber lip seal guarantees full bearing lubrication.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wrench-tightening crushes the rubber gasket and distorts the canister; oil filters should be oiled and tightened by hand to spec.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tightening a spin-on engine oil filter with a heavy metal strap wrench prevents high-pressure oil leaks around the base gasket.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Air directed from the outside drives fine grit deeper into the paper pores, whereas low-pressure air must blow from inside out.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Blowing compressed air from the dirty outside surface of a paper air filter toward the inside clears dust out of the pleats.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Air pockets in a diesel fuel system cause airlock and starve the injectors, so the primer pump and bleed screw must purge all air.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Replacing a diesel fuel filter without bleeding trapped air from the lines allows the injection pump to self-prime on startup.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to internal bearing races if a Scout pumps grease into a zerk fitting without wiping off the crusted dirt first?
Which physical indicator on the old oil filter housing must you verify before spinning on the new replacement filter?
Under what condition does blowing high-pressure shop air through a radiator or paper air filter element ruin the component?
Why is it dangerous to twist off a pressurized tractor radiator cap immediately after shutting down a hot diesel engine?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Agricultural machines often run at high load while stationary or moving slowly, so service intervals are tracked by engine hours.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tractor maintenance schedules should be tracked by calendar months or road miles just like a passenger car or pickup truck.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Substandard fluids lack the friction modifiers needed for wet clutches and brakes, causing chatter, glazing, and gear failure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cheaper universal tractor hydraulic fluid works identically to manufacturer-specified fluid in modern wet-brake transmissions.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Harvest downtime costs thousands of dollars per day in crop loss and emergency labor, dwarfing the cost of off-season maintenance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Waiting until a combine or planter breaks down in the field is cheaper than paying for preseason dealership inspection checklists.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Detergent additives in diesel oil are designed to hold soot in suspension, so laboratory oil analysis rather than color checks health.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dark black diesel engine oil on the dipstick proves the oil is worn out and has lost all of its lubricating additives.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms to a dealership technician whether used engine oil contains internal bearing wear metals or coolant leaks?
Under what condition does deferring a routine fluid and filter service cost a farmer far more than the price of the parts?
Which physical indicator on a diagnostic trouble code report helps a service manager trace intermittent implement sensor faults?
Where should a Scout record engine hour-meter readings and filter part numbers to keep a tractor's warranty valid at the dealer?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Flared and O-ring fittings seal on precision metal cones or elastomers, and loose tape shreds can contaminate hydraulic valves.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wrapping Teflon thread tape around JIC flared or O-ring boss hydraulic fittings stops stubborn high-pressure oil seepage.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Contact above the wheel centerline allows upward-moving bristles to catch the edge and hurl the metal part back at the operator.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Holding a small steel bracket above the horizontal centerline of a spinning wire wheel gives the cleanest rust removal angle.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The inner safety element protects the intake while the outer filter is removed and must be replaced, never cleaned or tapped.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tapping a dusty inner safety air filter element against a shop bench or tire cleans it for reuse alongside the primary filter.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hydraulic fluid escaping a pinhole at 2,000 PSI pierces skin and leather, causing severe tissue necrosis that requires surgery.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pinholes in a high-pressure hydraulic hose only spray harmless oil mist that can be wiped off with a gloved hand while running.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to sweep your bare fingers along a hydraulic hose to search for a pinhole fluid leak under pressure?
Where should a Scout position a metal workpiece against a rotating bench wire wheel so the bristles do not snatch the part?
Which physical indicator inside a bright flashlight beam reveals that a paper air filter element has a pinhole tear?
What happens to a flared JIC hydraulic fitting if a mechanic wraps PTFE thread tape around the flare cone before tightening?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Today's agricultural technicians troubleshoot CAN-bus networks, GPS autosteering, telemetry modems, and Tier 4 emissions systems.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern farm equipment mechanics only need basic hand tools and mechanical wrenching skills because tractors have simple engines.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most master dealership technicians earn a two-year associate degree in diesel technology combined with manufacturer apprenticeships.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A four-year university engineering degree is required before anyone can qualify as a certified dealership service technician.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Field technicians operate service trucks with cranes, welders, and compressors while managing weather, mud, and remote safety risks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mobile agricultural mechanics perform the exact same tasks in a farmer's field as technicians working inside a dealership bay.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Agricultural engineers design and test new machinery systems, whereas technicians diagnose, calibrate, and repair field equipment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Agricultural engineering and farm equipment technician careers are identical roles that share the same daily shop duties.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms that a precision agriculture specialist has calibrated a tractor's RTK GPS receiver to centimeter accuracy?
Under what condition does a mobile field service technician need both CAN-bus laptop diagnostics and heavy rigging certifications?
Which physical indicator on a dynamometer test run verifies that an overhauled diesel tractor engine meets factory PTO horsepower?
Where should a Scout gain hands-on shop hours and manufacturer credentials before applying for an implement dealership apprenticeship?
